{{Short description|Japanese mathematician}}
'''Hitoshi Kumano-Go''' (4 October 1935 – 24 August 1982) was a Japanese mathematician who specialized in [[partial differential equation]]s. He is especially recognized for his work on [[pseudo-differential operator]]s and [[Fourier integral operator]]s.

== Life ==
Hitoshi Kumano-go was born on 4 October 1935 in Arita, [[Wakayama Prefecture]]. After finishing high school in 1954, he studied mathematics and graduated from [[Osaka University]] in 1958. He started a doctoral work at the same university under the supervision of [[Mitio Nagumo]]. He received his PhD in 1963. He was promoted to associate professor in 1967 and to full professorship in 1971.<ref name="Tanabe 1983">{{Cite journal|last=Tanabe|first=Hiroki|date=1983|title=Hitoshi Kumano-go: 1935--1982|url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ojm/1200775811|journal=Osaka Journal of Mathematics|language=EN|volume=20|issue=1|pages=i–vii|issn=0030-6126}}</ref> From 1967 to 1969, Kumano-go had been a visiting member at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] of New York University. In May 1981 he entered Osaka University Hospital where a [[brain tumor]] was discovered. Kumano-go died on 24 August 1982 in Osaka at the age of 46.<ref name="Tanabe 1983" />

== Work ==
Kumano-Go first studied the local and global uniqueness of the solutions of the [[Cauchy problem]] for partial differential equations.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kumano-go|first=Hitoshi|date=1962|title=On the uniqueness of the solution of the Cauchy problem and the unique continuation theorem for elliptic equation|url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ojm/1200690503|journal=Osaka Mathematical Journal|language=EN|volume=14|issue=1|pages=181–212|issn=0388-0699}}</ref> While at the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Kumano-Go collaborated with [[Kurt Otto Friedrichs|Kurt Friedrichs]], [[Peter Lax]] and [[Louis Nirenberg]] among others. He made major contributions to the theory of pseudo-differential operators. Its work contributed to the construction of the fundamental solution of a first order [[Hyperbolic system|hyperbolic partial differential equation]].<ref name="Tanabe 1983" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kumano-Go|first=Hitoshi|date=1977|title=Fundamental solutions for operators of regularly hyperbolic type|url=https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jmath1948/29/3/29_3_399/_article/-char/ja/|journal=Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan|language=en|volume=29|issue=3|pages=399–406|doi=10.2969/jmsj/02930399|issn=0025-5645|doi-access=free}}</ref> His treatise on pseudo differential operators was first published in Japanese in 1974 and translated into English in 1981.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Pseudo-differential operators|last=Kumano-go|first=Hitoshi|date=1982|publisher=MIT Press|isbn=978-0-262-11080-8|location=Cambridge, Massachusetts|oclc=8386677}}</ref><ref name="Tanabe 1983" />

Kumano-Go also made important contribution to the study of Fourier integral operators.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kumano-go|first=Hitoshi|date=1976|title=A calculus of Fourier integral operators on Rn and the fundamental solution for an operator of hyperbolic type|journal=Communications in Partial Differential Equations|language=en|volume=1|issue=1|pages=1–44|doi=10.1080/03605307608820002|issn=0360-5302}}</ref>
